name: Filter House
about: Filter house is the disco-loop strain of house that defined the late 1990s: a bar or two of an old disco or boogie record, looped and swept with a resonant low-pass filter so the track seems to open and close like a door, over a compressed four-to-the-floor kick. Daft Punk's Homework and Thomas Bangalter's Roulé label gave it a Paris address, and Stardust's Music Sounds Better with You made it a worldwide pop sound in 1998; Armand Van Helden, Phats & Small and Modjo took it to the charts while Alan Braxe and Fred Falke refined it. It burned out as a mainstream style by 2002 but never left DJ sets, and the future funk producers of the 2010s rebuilt it from Japanese city pop.

artists.name: Fred Falke
artists.why: live bass under the filtered loop

artists.name: Bob Sinclar
artists.why: took filtered disco to French radio

albums.title: Blue Funk Files
albums.why: Before Paris, Chicago: Sneak's Henry Street debut is where the filtered disco loop first became a house producer's whole method.

albums.title: Super Discount
albums.why: The French Touch's first filter-house classic, with Prix Choc sweeping a disco loop open and shut over a kick that defined the next five years.

albums.title: Sacrebleu
albums.why: Less filter than disco scholarship, but Dimitri's debut taught the Paris scene how to loop old records with affection rather than irony.

albums.title: Homework
albums.why: Da Funk, Around the World and Revolution 909 are filter house as raw, jacking Chicago tribute; the record every producer in this style copied.

albums.title: Paradise
albums.why: Gym Tonic and My Only Love made Sinclar's debut the filtered-disco record French radio loved; glossy, catchy and a little thin.

albums.title: 2 Future 4 U
albums.why: U Don't Know Me and Flowerz are filter house at American volume, and the album around them is Van Helden's loudest and most fun.

albums.title: Now Phats What I Small Call Music
albums.why: Turn Around made the Brighton duo filter house's British face, and the album stretches the trick about as far as it goes.
Zdar and Boombass's filtered-disco pop record, with Feeling for You and the title track; the French Touch at its most direct.

albums.title: Darkdancer
albums.why: Stuart Price's fake-French album crossed filter house with 1980s synth-pop, and Jacques Your Body is still the style's wittiest single.

albums.title: Remedy
albums.why: Brixton's answer to Paris: Red Alert and Rendez-Vu borrow the filtered loop and then throw ragga, Latin and punk at it; the decade's best house album.

albums.title: Crydamoure Presents Waves
albums.why: Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo's label collected on one disc, Le Knight Club and Paul Johnson's filtered disco at its purest.

albums.title: Tempovision
albums.why: De Crécy's solo album moves the Super Discount loop into a darker, more melodic place, with Am I Wrong as the keeper.

albums.title: Champs Elysées
albums.why: I Feel for You is the hit and Darlin' the deep cut; the album is Sinclar's filter-disco formula at its most commercial.

albums.title: Discovery
albums.why: One More Time, Digital Love and Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger turned the filter trick into pop art, and nothing in the style has matched it.

albums.title: Modjo
albums.why: Lady, built on a filtered Chic loop, is the style's biggest single, and Romain Tranchart's album has more real songs than its reputation allows.

albums.title: Midnight Funk
albums.why: A late French Touch record that keeps the grit on its filtered funk loops; You Are My High is the one DJs still reach for.

albums.title: Gourmet de Funk
albums.why: The Hanover producer's debut collects his disco-house hits, Horny and Sex Bomb among them; cheerful, polished and not deep.

albums.title: The Upper Cuts
albums.why: Braxe and Fred Falke's singles gathered together, Intro and Rubicon included; the Roulé-school filter sound refined into bass-led pop.

albums.title: Idiosyncrasies
albums.why: The German producer's debut is a late revival of the Braxe and Falke sound, filtered disco with 1980s synth gloss and real care.

albums.title: Part IV
albums.why: Falke's long-delayed solo album turns his bass-guitar filter house toward soft rock and synth-pop; pleasant, more remixer than songwriter.

albums.title: By Your Side
albums.why: Ed Banger's disco revivalist brought the filtered loop back with live bass and falsetto hooks; Baby I'm Yours is the keeper.

albums.title: Hit Vibes
albums.why: The future funk record that rebuilt filter house from Japanese city pop loops, and the template for an internet scene that followed.

note: The style's defining records were 12-inch singles such as Stardust, Spiller and Room 5, so this shelf leans on the albums around them.
